tools.name: react_get_tree
tools.title: React component tree
tools.description: Get the live React component tree as a flat node list (id, parentId, name, key, kind). Reconstruct the hierarchy from parentId; pass node ids to react_inspect_component. For a dense tree, pass a returned node id as rootId to read that component and its descendants without dumping unrelated branches. Framework wrappers can be deep, so raise `depth` if your own components do not appear and `truncatedBy` is "depth". `otherRoots` lists separate React roots (widgets bundling their own React, createRoot islands); pass one's rootId to read it. Arguments: depth: minimum 1, maximum 80; maxNodes: minimum 1, maximum 2000.

rootId.description: Read only this mounted component/host node and its descendants. The selected node is included with parentId:null. Omit for the full root.

includeHost.description: Include host (DOM) elements, not just components.

appOnly.description: Include only proven app ownership when true; library and unknown ownership are excluded with coverage. False includes all ownership classes.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_get_tree --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_provenance
tools.title: React provenance health
tools.description: Scan a bounded set of mounted components and report recursive wrapper ancestry, app/library/unknown ownership, split source roles, source-map confidence, and explicit failure reasons. This diagnostic never promotes an ambiguous fallback to a definition or allocation callsite. Arguments: limit: minimum 1, maximum 500.

appOnly.description: When true, include only components with resolved app ownership.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_provenance --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_find_components
tools.title: Find React components
tools.description: Find mounted components by display name (substring match, or exact) across every live React root, including widgets that bundle their own React. Each match carries its id, ancestor path, kind, a shallow (depth-1) props preview, source file:line, and whether it is a library component — enough to pick the right one and often to act without a follow-up react_inspect_component call. Deepen a nested prop with react_inspect_component + `path`. Arguments: component: minimum characters 1; query: minimum characters 1; limit: minimum 1, maximum 200.

query.description: Deprecated alias for component. Provide component or query; both must agree.

appOnly.description: Include only proven app ownership when true; library and unknown ownership are excluded with coverage. False includes all ownership classes.

tools.name: react_inspect_component
tools.title: Inspect a React component
tools.description: Inspect a component by id: its props, plus state (class components) or hooks (function components), depth-bounded. Each hook reports its `kind` (state/reducer/effect/layout-effect/memo/callback/ref/other), whether it is `stateful`, for stateful hooks a `stateIndex` — the ordinal you pass to react_override_hook_state instead of counting flat hook positions past library hooks — and `customHooks`, the custom-hook chain that called it (e.g. ["useCart","useQuery"]), so you can tell which hook to edit. Functions appear as their `ƒ name()` preview string. Pass `path` to hydrate deeper into a nested prop value. Arguments: depth: minimum 1, maximum 6.

path.description: Path into props to hydrate deeper, e.g. ["user","address"].

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_inspect_component --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_override_props
tools.title: Override component props (dev)
tools.description: Live-edit a mounted component's props by id (dev only): merges the given partial props and triggers a re-render. Useful for testing UI states.

tools.name: react_override_hook_state
tools.title: Override hook state (dev)
tools.description: Set a stateful hook's value and re-render — drive a function component into any state (a wizard step, an open modal, an invalid form) without a multi-step UI script. Target the hook with EXACTLY ONE of: `stateIndex` (the 0-based ordinal among only the stateful useState/useReducer hooks — the `stateIndex` react_inspect_component prints on each stateful hook, robust to library hooks shifting flat positions) or `hookIndex` (the raw flat index over ALL hooks). Prefer stateIndex. Only stateful hooks can be overridden; a failed call lists the stateful hooks (flat index, stateIndex, kind, value preview) so you can retry. `path` targets a nested field of the value (e.g. ["filters","page"]); omit it to replace the whole value. The component's own next setState takes back control; use react_reset_overrides to clear all overrides at once. Arguments: hookIndex: minimum 0, maximum 99; stateIndex: minimum 0, maximum 99.

hookIndex.description: Raw flat hook index over all hooks. Provide this OR stateIndex, not both.

stateIndex.description: Preferred. 0-based ordinal among only the stateful hooks, as react_inspect_component reports. Provide this OR hookIndex, not both.

path.description: Path into the hook value; empty replaces the whole value.

tools.name: react_override_context
tools.title: Override a context value (dev)
tools.description: Override a React Context for a whole subtree by editing the nearest Provider's `value` above a component — test a different theme/locale/flag without touching code. Pass the id of a component that consumes the context (react_inspect_context lists them; `context` picks one by name when it consumes several) or a Provider id directly. A plain-object `value` shallow-merges into the current value; any other value replaces it. Reverts when the Provider's parent re-renders — same lifetime as react_override_props. A context running on its default value (no Provider mounted) cannot be overridden.

context.description: Context displayName, from react_inspect_context — required when several are consumed.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_override_context --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_toggle_suspense_fallback
tools.title: Force a Suspense fallback (dev)
tools.description: Hold the nearest Suspense boundary at/above a component in its fallback (loading) state, or release it — a state normally visible for milliseconds becomes one you can inspect and screenshot to verify loading UI. Pass any component id inside the boundary, or a boundaryId from react_error_state. Persists until released with showFallback:false or a page reload. react_list_overrides shows every active override; react_reset_overrides releases them all at once (works even if this id no longer resolves).

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_toggle_suspense_fallback --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_force_error_boundary
tools.title: Force an error boundary (dev)
tools.description: Make the nearest error boundary at/above a component catch a simulated error, or release it — verify error UI renders and that the intended boundary contains the failure, without manufacturing a real crash. Pass any component id inside the boundary. Release with the returned boundaryId and forceError:false — the original child id unmounts while the boundary is erroring, so its id may no longer resolve on release; if you get "Component N not found", call react_reset_overrides, which clears forced errors from module state without needing the id. Caveat: if the BOUNDARY itself re-mounted while forced (React Native RedBox flows do this), the new instance stays latched in its error state after reset — reload the app to restore the UI. react_list_overrides shows what is currently forced.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_force_error_boundary --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_list_overrides
tools.title: List active overrides (dev)
tools.description: List every live override genie has applied and not yet reset — props, hook state, context, forced Suspense fallbacks, and forced error boundaries — with the target component, a human-readable detail (e.g. `title="GENIE OVERRIDE" (was "Activities")`, `hook 12 ← true`, `fallback forced`), and whether that target is still mounted. componentId is the live id when the target is still findable from the current root, else null with mounted:false (its subtree may have re-mounted with new ids). Use before react_reset_overrides to see what will be cleared.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_list_overrides --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: react_reset_overrides
tools.title: Reset all overrides (dev)
tools.description: Clear every override at once and return the app to its real state — the universal release and the recovery path when a forced-error/suspense boundary left the app stuck and the original id no longer resolves (react_force_error_boundary / react_toggle_suspense_fallback release by id, this does not need one). props, context, and hook overrides restore their captured pre-override value when the target is still mounted ("restored"); a hook target that unmounted or lost its renderer is "released" instead — the overridden value stays until the component's own next setState. Forced Suspense/error boundaries are released and re-rendered from module state even if unmounted. Each cleared override reports its outcome.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools react_reset_overrides --output-schema --session measure

Each element comes with a best-effort CSS `selector` plus its id / data-testid / role / aria-label / name / classes / text, so you can hand it straight to a browser tool (click, screenshot, assert) instead of guessing which node a component controls. `styleSources` lists the style definitions applied to the element (file:line, application order) when the app emits style provenance (e.g. StyleX dev mode). Arguments: limit: minimum 1, maximum 50.

tools.name: react_component_for_dom

tools.description: Map a CSS selector (e.g. an element a browser tool found) to the React component(s) rendering it — the reverse of react_dom_for_component, turning "this button is wrong" into "edit this component". Each match reports the owning component id (feed it to react_inspect_component / overrides), name, kind, shallow props, and source file:line, plus `styleSources` — the style definitions applied to the matched element (file:line, application order; later wins conflicts) when the app emits style provenance (e.g. StyleX dev mode), turning "this looks wrong" into "edit this style definition". Elements outside this React tree are skipped; duplicate owners are collapsed. Arguments: limit: minimum 1, maximum 20; propsDepth: minimum 0, maximum 4.

appOnly.description: Include only proven app ownership when true; library and unknown ownership are excluded with coverage. False includes all ownership classes.

durationMs.description: How long to sample. Longer is steadier; 5000ms suits most interactions.

tools.name: plugin_list
tools.title: List DevTools plugins
tools.description: List every TanStack DevTools plugin (built-in and third-party) that has emitted traffic on the client event bus, with how many recent events each has buffered. Discovery is traffic-based — a plugin only appears after its first event — except ids declared via <Genie plugins>, which are listed immediately with eventCount 0 until traffic arrives. Use a pluginId with plugin_get_events.

tools.title: Get plugin events
tools.description: Get the most recent buffered events for one DevTools plugin by pluginId, newest last. Payloads are depth-bounded. Use plugin_list to discover plugin ids. Nested synchronous dispatch can buffer a response BEFORE the request that triggered it, so read a wide `limit` and do not assume request-then-response order.

tools.title: Emit a plugin event
tools.description: Emit an event onto the TanStack DevTools event bus so browser plugins receive it. `type` may be bare ("refresh") or fully qualified ("my-plugin:refresh") — a bare type is prefixed with `pluginId` automatically, matching what listeners subscribe to. Returns ok=false when no DevTools bus is present.

tools.name: timeline_start
tools.title: Start interaction timeline
tools.description: Begin an on-demand bounded recording of request completions, Query updates, React root commits and TanStack navigation on one monotonic clock. Temporal correlation only, not causation. No listeners run before this call. One recording is retained; starting replaces a stopped recording. Automatically stops at the event or duration limit.

next.command: pnpm exec genie-react tools timeline_start --output-schema --session measure

tools.name: timeline_read
tools.title: Read interaction timeline
tools.description: Read a bounded page in stable observation order, optionally filtered by domain. Keep the same domains while paginating. Resource start/end times are separate from asynchronous observation time. Coverage explains missing evidence. A null nextOffset means caught up now; an active recording can append more events.

tools.name: timeline_stop
tools.title: Stop interaction timeline
tools.description: Stop recording, flush queued request timing entries, unsubscribe all sources and retain a frozen report. Repeated stops return the same report. Use timeline_read to retrieve events.

tools.name: devtools_status

tools.description: Block until a runtime condition holds so the agent can synchronize instead of polling. `settled` reports each requested React, Query, Router, frame, or optional network domain independently; partial quiet never collapses into idle. For queries, prefer queryHash or queryKey from query_list; legacy matching is exact.

name.description: Component name or route. For query-settled, a legacy exact queryHash, JSON array key, or one-item string key; prefer queryHash/queryKey.

tools.description: Wait until no React document commit is observed for idleMs. Returns idle, timed-out, or unavailable with elapsed time and commits observed since the first valid sample. Does not establish query, animation-frame, or future scheduled work completion. Session changes or counter resets cannot prove idle. Arguments: idleMs: minimum 100, maximum 5000; timeoutMs: maximum 60000, greater than 0.

tools.name: devtools_capture_create
tools.title: Create an immutable runtime capture
tools.description: Create and retain a named, schema-versioned artifact containing bounded runtime sections. The bridge probes React commits before and after, retries when they move, and records whether the final artifact is React-commit-stable or best-effort. Returns the capture summary by default; read sections later with devtools_capture_read or export the artifact with `genie-react capture export`.

include.description: Domains to capture. Defaults to whichever of react, effects, query, router, and memory the app advertises.

view.description: summary (default) returns bounded decision fields; full returns the retained artifact with every section.

tools.name: devtools_capture_list
tools.title: List retained runtime captures
tools.description: List bounded capture summaries newest first. The bridge retains at most 20 captures; export important artifacts from devtools_capture_create/read as JSON.

tools.name: devtools_capture_read
tools.title: Read an immutable runtime capture
tools.description: Read one retained capture by exact ID. The default summary view is bounded; request full or selected sections only when needed.

view.description: summary (default) returns bounded decision fields; full returns the retained artifact.

sections.description: For view="full", include only these sections.

tools.name: devtools_capture_pin
tools.title: Pin or unpin a retained capture
tools.description: Protect a capture from retention eviction, or unpin it. When all retained slots are pinned, creating another capture is refused instead of deleting evidence.

tools.name: devtools_capture_compare
tools.title: Compare repeated runtime captures
tools.description: Compare repeated baseline and candidate capture cohorts with median, p95, and median absolute deviation (MAD). Apply optional typed regression budgets per metric. At least minimumRuns usable samples per cohort are required for a pass/fail budget verdict; smaller or missing cohorts remain explicit insufficient-data. Capture IDs must be unique and cannot appear in both cohorts.

tools.name: devtools_interaction_begin
tools.title: Begin an atomic interaction observation
tools.description: Clear and start one targeted React observation under a bridge-owned interaction ID. Only one interaction may record per physical app document; drive the UI, then call devtools_interaction_stop to freeze and read one bounded bundle.

tools.name: devtools_interaction_stop
tools.title: Stop and read an atomic interaction observation
tools.description: Freeze React profiling before waiting, then summarize the interaction: top rendered components with their most frequent cause, the hottest effects, cohorts, settle and coverage. Commits occurring during settle are excluded by the profile freeze and counted explicitly. Repeat the call with view:"full" (optionally with sections) to read the retained renders, causes, effects and cohort evidence.

view.description: summary (default) returns bounded decision fields; full returns the retained renders, causes, effects and cohort tool results.

sections.description: For view="full", include only these sections.
